profile.reading:
This Lumen colocation facility, internally identified in public records as San Antonio 2, is located at 215 Rivas Street, San Antonio, TX 78207, in Bexar County; Lumen does not publish individual building addresses or specs on its own site for any of its 175-plus North American colocation sites. Lumen Technologies, formerly CenturyLink (renamed Lumen on September 14, 2020, with its stock ticker changing from CTL to LUMN on September 18, 2020) and built in part on CenturyLink's November 1, 2017 acquisition of Level 3 Communications, operates this facility as part of a network-centric edge colocation product rather than a wholesale hyperscale campus. Lumen's own colocation data sheet states more than 175 carrier-neutral data centers across more than 60 North American markets, offering cabinet power in the 3 to 15 kilowatt range described as varying by site; unlike the wholesale operators tracked elsewhere in this registry, Lumen does not disclose per-building square footage or total MW capacity for any of its sites.

Texas's data center sales tax exemption cost the state roughly $5-30 million a year from 2014 through 2022, jumped to more than $150 million in 2023, and is now projected at $1.3 billion for the current fiscal year, $3.2 billion over 2026-2028, and nearly $1.8 billion annually by fiscal 2030, according to the Texas Tribune. Separately, ERCOT's interconnection queue holds roughly 474 gigawatts of pending requests, more than five times the grid's record peak demand, with Governor Abbott stating about 90% of new power requests are data centers; Abbott ordered an audit of queued data centers in August 2026, and ERCOT sought a delay of its transmission planning study from the Public Utility Commission the same month. San Antonio's municipally owned utility, CPS Energy, has separately fielded its own wave of large-load interconnection requests tied to data center development in the metro area.

reading.body:
Lumen San Antonio 2 sits in Bexar County at coordinates that place it in San Antonio proper. The facility's IT capacity is not published by the operator. Without a published power figure or a dedicated product page, this campus cannot be ranked among the state's disclosed capacity, though it is mapped as an existing Lumen location.

Texas has 133 mapped data center facilities, of which 18 publish power capacity totaling 468 megawatts. This campus ranks 19th by published megawatts in the state, which means it either publishes no figure or publishes below the threshold of the mapped facilities that do. The state context suggests most mapped facilities in Texas disclose nothing about their scale.

Whether this facility is part of Lumen's current colocation product line, retained from before the 2017 sale of the company's data center business to Cyxtera, or acquired or rebuilt after that divestiture, is not established in available sources. The operator's own pages do not confirm this location's current role, power capacity, or qualification for AI workloads.
